headline: High: Pipecat’s shared-bus, networked defaults can amplify ComfyUI outputs into unsafe downstream actions; data leakage and compliance risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/shared filesystem bridge, so direct prompt injection into it is blocked. Pipecat, however, uses a shared bus and stdin/stdout, so if an operator manually forwards ComfyUI text or metadata into Pipecat, instruction-like content could be misread. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI-generated text into Pipecat inputs, THEN instruction-like payloads can be parsed downstream.
IF a shared bus or wrapper forwards ComfyUI metadata into Pipecat without provenance tags, THEN injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs as images only; do not paste generated text into Pipecat.
Add a manual review step before any Pipecat prompt or tool call.
Prefix all bridged content as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, seeds, checkpoints, and embeddings, while Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state. Pipecat’s allowlisted egress and shared-bus model make leakage plausible if ComfyUI artifacts are passed into its pipeline. ComfyUI is offline by default, but the pair still creates a default path for sensitive media to reach external services through Pipecat.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are routed into Pipecat sessions, THEN media or seed data can leave the local boundary.
IF Pipecat is configured with external STT/LLM/TTS/image services, THEN bridged content may be transmitted off-host.
mitigations: Do not route checkpoints, seeds, or embeddings into Pipecat.
Use a local-only Pipecat configuration for any bridged media.
Disable external STT/LLM/TTS providers for sensitive sessions.
Review logs for accidental media capture.
requires-engineering: segregate workspaces and network paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI can write model files locally, while Pipecat supports multiple instances on a shared bus and can operate across processes or machines. There is no explicit locking or shared-write protection between them, so if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or asset directory, they can overwrite or race on shared artifacts. The conflict is plausible but not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same asset directory, THEN file races or overwrites can occur.
IF Pipecat instances share a bus while ComfyUI updates model assets, THEN stale or conflicting state can be observed.
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent.
Make shared assets read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes during active sessions.
Check for duplicate filenames before syncing.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate images and workflow artifacts that Pipecat may consume as part of audio/video/text sessions. Pipecat’s broad service integrations mean it could act on those outputs without strong verification unless the operator adds one. That makes misgenerated or manipulated ComfyUI outputs capable of cascading into downstream responses or actions.
conditions: IF Pipecat treats ComfyUI outputs as authoritative inputs, THEN downstream responses can propagate errors.
IF Pipecat is connected to action-taking services or external APIs, THEN a bad ComfyUI output can cascade further.
mitigations: Require human review of ComfyUI outputs before Pipecat uses them.
Add validation for image/text payloads before downstream use.
Log source provenance on every bridged artifact.
Limit Pipecat to read-only consumption of generated media.
requires-engineering: add schema checks and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and local, but Pipecat commonly sends audio, text, and media to third-party STT/LLM/TTS services over allowlisted egress. If regulated or sensitive media produced by ComfyUI is bridged into Pipecat, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF bridged content includes regulated personal data, THEN Pipecat service routing may create residency or retention mismatch.
IF external providers are enabled in Pipecat, THEN compliance obligations can differ from ComfyUI's local-only handling.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the bridge.
Use only local providers for Pipecat on sensitive workloads.
Document retention settings for each external service.
Review whether any data class requires residency controls.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and deletion workflows.
